text.p: Brazilian private steelmaker Acesita issued the following statement on its 1996 results.
NOTE: All data above in Brazil's real. Figures were calculated under inflation-adjusted accounting method.
Under the Brazilian corporate law accounting method, the company said it posted a net profit of 2.8 million reais last year against 30.9 million reais in 1995.

In a statement, Acesita's financial and Investor Relations director Luiz Anibal de Lima Fernandes attributed the firm's lower profits to a 17-percent drop in international stainless steel prices, higher prices of raw materials and lower demand in the domestic market.
Acesita said it sold 543,300 tonnes of steel last year, up from 542,500 tonnes in 1995. Of that total, 21.8 percent were exported mainly to the United States, Hungary, Hong Kong and Argentina.
Stainless steel accounted for 16,200 tonnes sold, it added.
Acesita said it has approved payment of a 0.01 real dividend per 1,000 stocks equivalent to 62 percent of the firm's profits in 1996.
The company also said it will invest 150 million reais in 1997, of which 95 million reais in expanding its stainless steel output.
